entries.authors: Wang, P., Li, Y., Tian, Y.
entries.difference: Reframes agent security as an agent-human interaction problem and reports, from a survey of production systems, that runtime approval is deployed while no criterion for when a gate pays exists; it names the deployment and leaves the criterion open, which is this study's question.
entries.pool_title: Reframing LLM Agent Security as an Agent-Human Interaction Problem
entries.title: Reframing LLM Agent Security as an Agent-Human Interaction Problem

entries.difference: Surveys authorization architectures for tool-using agents and organises them by where the check sits; it compares architectures as designs, and measures no value for a gate, so the fidelity at which a gate's value turns negative is not a quantity in it.
entries.pool_title: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents
entries.title: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents

entries.authors: Chidambaram, N., Tosi, M., Cabot, J.
entries.difference: Measures publication and adoption of the Model Context Protocol across two dimensions; its unit is a protocol's uptake, not the net value of a human approval step over a channel.
entries.pool_title: A Two-Dimensional Study of the Model Context Protocol: Publication and Adoption
entries.title: A Two-Dimensional Study of the Model Context Protocol: Publication and Adoption

entries.difference: Characterises centralization and observability of the remote MCP ecosystem by measurement; observability of a tool transport is a different object from the fidelity of the artifact a reviewer is shown.
entries.pool_title: Characterizing Network Centralization and Observability in the Remote MCP Ecosystem
entries.title: Characterizing Network Centralization and Observability in the Remote MCP Ecosystem

entries.difference: Translates EU AI Act obligations into executable compliance pipelines, i.e. a governance-as-code reading of oversight; compliance is asserted by a pipeline, while this study asks whether the human step it mandates has positive expected value.
entries.pool_title: Governance-as-Code: Translating EU AI Act Technical Requirements into Executable Compliance Pipelines for Generative AI Systems
entries.title: Governance-As-Code: Translating EU AI Act Technical Requirements into Executable Compliance Pipelines for Generative AI Systems

entries.difference: Proposes a theory of governed proactive agency with human control in the loop; it is a design theory, and it fixes no parameter at which oversight stops paying.
entries.pool_title: When Intelligence Becomes Agency: A Theory of Governed, Proactive Agency for Symbiotic AI Systems
entries.title: When Intelligence Becomes Agency: A Theory of Governed, Proactive Agency for Symbiotic AI Systems

entries.difference: Gives an architecture for long-horizon agents built on levels and ticks, in which approval is one scheduling event; scheduling an approval is not the same as pricing it.
entries.pool_title: An Architecture for Long-Horizon Agents: Levels, Ticks and Cascaded Intelligence
entries.title: An Architecture for Long-Horizon Agents: Levels, Ticks and Cascaded Intelligence

entries.difference: Finds that human capital rather than model benchmarks predicts hybrid human-AI forecasting gain; it measures the human's contribution as a population property, and our construct is whether the object the human is shown denotes the object that executes.
entries.pool_title: Human Capital, Not Model Benchmarks, Predicts Hybrid Intelligence in Forecasting
entries.title: Human Capital, Not Model Benchmarks, Predicts Hybrid Intelligence in Forecasting

entries.difference: Poses an enterprise governance kernel in which tool invocations are policy-mediated; a policy kernel decides what is permitted, and the question here is what a gate is worth when the object it reviews is not the object it authorises.
entries.pool_title: A Unified Policy Architecture (UPA): The Governance Kernel for Enterprise AI Operating Systems
entries.title: A Unified Policy Architecture (UPA): The Governance Kernel for Enterprise AI Operating Systems

entries.authors: Vallabhaneni, U., Cagwin, C., Wild, D.
entries.difference: Offloads topological reasoning from LLM agents in a security operations centre, where analyst escalation is a routine step; escalation volume is treated as load to reduce rather than as a cost term that can exceed the harm a gate prevents.
entries.pool_title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center
entries.title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center

entries.difference: Calibrates agent guards to a subjective, fatiguing human and shows oversight has a capacity; it prices the reviewer's capacity, and our model keeps the reviewer fixed and varies the channel's fidelity, so the two are complementary inputs to one value.
entries.pool_title: Oversight Has a Capacity: Calibrating Agent Guards to a Subjective, Fatiguing Human
entries.title: Oversight Has a Capacity: Calibrating Agent Guards to a Subjective, Fatiguing Human

entries.difference: Measures constraint weakening across 1,296 controlled episodes, where a normal handoff transform deactivates binding state in 100.0% of them and 54.2% of downstream executions perform a forbidden action; it measures that fidelity is below 1 in an ordinary pipeline, which this study takes as the low end of its axis rather than as its question.
entries.pool_title: When "Must" Becomes "Maybe": Constraint Weakening in LLM Agent Workflows
entries.title: When "Must" Becomes "Maybe": Constraint Weakening in LLM Agent Workflows

entries.difference: Reproduces approval hijacking across agent frameworks and reports attack success without binding versus with it; it establishes the failure exists and that binding removes it, and does not give a value for the gate as a function of the fidelity that binds it.
entries.pool_title: Loopjacking: Hijacking Human-in-the-Loop Approval
entries.title: Loopjacking: Hijacking Human-In-The-Loop Approval

entries.difference: Binds an action to a verifiable card and reports 68-100% attack success unbound against 0% bound with a 0% false-block rate; those are the endpoints of this study's fidelity axis, read here as inputs to a value law rather than as a defence evaluation.
entries.pool_title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
entries.title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-In-The-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents

entries.authors: Shraga, I., Eshel, R., Gorelik, L.
entries.difference: Shows an LLM guardrail can approve correctly at check time and be stale by act time; staleness is the time axis of the same defect this study writes as a substitution channel, and it measures staleness rather than the value of the gate that suffers it.
entries.pool_title: Approved Too Late: Verdict Staleness in LLM-Guarded Self-Adaptive Systems
entries.title: Approved Too Late: Verdict Staleness in LLM-Guarded Self-Adaptive Systems

entries.difference: Identifies decision conflicts for long-running agents whose authorising state changes after the check, and proposes selective revalidation; revalidation is a repair, and this study gives the threshold on the fidelity axis at which a repair is worth its cost.
entries.pool_title: From Version Conflicts to Decision Conflicts: Selective Revalidation for Long-Running AI Agents
entries.title: From Version Conflicts to Decision Conflicts: Selective Revalidation for Long-Running AI Agents

entries.difference: Exposes UI desynchronization between what a mobile agent sees and what it acts on; that is a representation mismatch measured as a vulnerability class, where our model makes it a continuous fidelity parameter with a sign law.
entries.pool_title: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
entries.title: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents

entries.difference: Closes the time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap in root-of-trust protected systems at the hardware boundary; the mechanism is a trusted subsystem, whereas this study's subject is a human reviewer whose view of the object can be unfaithful.
entries.pool_title: SILK: Closing the Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use Gap in RoT-Protected AI Systems
entries.title: SILK: Closing the Time-Of-Check-To-Time-Of-Use Gap in RoT-Protected AI Systems

entries.difference: Argues authority should be held by a substrate other than the agent's own context, with a cross-substrate notion of authority; it settles where authority should live, not what an approval step is worth once authority has been placed.
entries.pool_title: From Evidence to Effect: Authority Semantics and Runtime Infrastructure for Stateful Agents
entries.title: From Evidence to Effect: Authority Semantics and Runtime Infrastructure for Stateful Agents

entries.difference: Studies trust propagation and structural containment in multi-agent pipelines, where a low-privilege agent can influence a high-privilege one; influence propagation across agents is a different channel from the fidelity with which one approval denotes its action.
entries.pool_title: Trust propagation and structural containment in Multi-agent LLM pipelines
entries.title: Trust Propagation and Structural Containment in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines

entries.authors: Huang, S., Zhang, J., Jia, H.
entries.difference: Shows malicious instructions can persist in agent memory and re-enter later execution; persistence is a temporal channel, and its harm is not modulated by the fidelity of any single approval.
entries.pool_title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents
entries.title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents

entries.difference: Audits candidate actions before execution to block indirect-injection consequences; a pre-execution audit is a programmatic check, which is one of the repairs this study prices against a reviewer-mediated one.
entries.pool_title: ActGuard: Pre-execution Action Auditing against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
entries.title: ActGuard: Pre-Execution Action Auditing Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents

entries.difference: Systematizes six ways a harness can dispatch an action other than the one a human approved and measures a bound-gap rate for each in one harness, then prototypes a keyed token as a binding defence; it measures and defends the failure, where this study takes binding fidelity as a parameter of a value functional and derives the fidelity below which the gate's net value turns negative, the accuracy-insensitivity that survives there, and the equivalence of the repair.
entries.pool_title: Approval Laundering: Systematizing Approval--Execution Binding Failures in AI Coding-Agent Harnesses
entries.title: Approval Laundering: Systematizing Approval--Execution Binding Failures in AI Coding-Agent Harnesses

entries.difference: Gives defences for tool-integrated agents against adversarial tool outputs; it measures blocking effectiveness, and this study measures when a human-mediated step is worth its own cost, including when it is worth less than no step.
entries.pool_title: Universal Defenses for Tool-Integrated LLM Agents Against Adversarial Attacks
entries.title: Universal Defenses for Tool-Integrated LLM Agents Against Adversarial Attacks

entries.authors: Zhang, Y., Huang, J., Gu, G.
entries.difference: Separates trust boundaries with provenance-aware transformers; provenance is a property the model is trained to use, while this study treats the reviewer's information as a channel whose fidelity is an experimental axis.
entries.pool_title: Origin Is All You Need: Provenance-Aware Transformers for Structural Trust-Boundary Separation
entries.title: Origin Is All You Need: Provenance-Aware Transformers for Structural Trust-Boundary Separation

entries.difference: Measures and exploits implicit trust in LLM tool-calling pipelines, including a protocol's trust assumptions; the trust measured is the model's, not the reviewer's, and no approval value is derived.
entries.pool_title: Measuring and Exploiting Implicit Trust in LLM Tool-Calling Pipelines
entries.title: Measuring and Exploiting Implicit Trust in LLM Tool-Calling Pipelines

entries.difference: Finds that instruction arbitration in agents is configuration-dependent and that recognition does not imply enforcement; the gap between recognising and enforcing is the same family as a mismatch channel, measured as a failure mode rather than as a fidelity parameter.
entries.pool_title: Recognition Without Enforcement: Configuration-Dependent Failures in LLM Agent Instruction Arbitration and External Control
entries.title: Recognition Without Enforcement: Configuration-Dependent Failures in LLM Agent Instruction Arbitration and External Control

entries.difference: Resolves tool names in a closed world to stop hallucinated calls; a hallucinated tool is not an approved object that failed to denote its action, so the defect it repairs is upstream of the approval channel.
entries.pool_title: Closed-World Resolution Against Tool Hallucination in LLM Agents
entries.title: Closed-World Resolution Against Tool Hallucination in LLM Agents

entries.difference: Shows multimodal GUI agents are distracted by environmental content; distraction is an input-side effect on the agent, whereas this study's channel carries the object to a human.
entries.pool_title: Caution for the Environment: Multimodal LLM Agents are Susceptible to Environmental Distractions
entries.title: Caution for the Environment: Multimodal LLM Agents Are Susceptible to Environmental Distractions

entries.difference: Trains GUI agents towards faithful behaviour rather than memorised shortcuts; it makes the agent's action faithful to the task, and our fidelity is between the object a reviewer approves and the object the system executes.
entries.pool_title: Faithful Mobile GUI Agents with Guided Advantage Estimator
entries.title: Faithful Mobile GUI Agents with Guided Advantage Estimator

entries.difference: Stress-tests long-horizon multi-agent systems adversarially so failures propagate through memory and tools; it reports propagation, where this study gives a value law for one gate at one fidelity.
entries.pool_title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
entries.title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems

entries.difference: Binds an agent's intent with cryptographically verifiable guardrails; the binding is verified cryptographically, which is the b = 1 end of this study's axis rather than a quantity computed across it.
entries.pool_title: NiyamAI - An Intent-Bound AI Agent with Cryptographically Verifiable Guardrails using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
entries.title: NiyamAI - an Intent-Bound AI Agent with Cryptographically Verifiable Guardrails Using Zero-Knowledge Proofs

entries.difference: Confines reachable capabilities for LLM agents under indirect injection, at the level of what a compromised agent can reach; capability reach is a bound on harm, and the value of an approval gate is a different quantity, which this study makes depend on fidelity.
entries.pool_title: Reachability-Based Capability Confinement for LLM Agents under Indirect Prompt Injection
entries.title: Reachability-Based Capability Confinement for LLM Agents under Indirect Prompt Injection

entries.authors: Veski, R., Guerraoui, R., Froelicher, D.
entries.difference: Delegates privileges among collaborating agents with a capability-based scheme; delegation governs who may act, while the question here is whether the object presented for review denotes the action taken.
entries.pool_title: CAPMAS: Capability-Based Delegation of Privileges in Multi-Agent Systems
entries.title: CAPMAS: Capability-Based Delegation of Privileges in Multi-Agent Systems

entries.authors: Gong, H., Samawi, M., Medda, F.
entries.difference: Separates inference from authority in agentic finance, so that a model's suggestion cannot confer authorisation; that separation is a policy design, and this study quantifies the step that implements it.
entries.pool_title: Authority-Inference Separation in Agentic Finance: First-Line Control, Blockchain Enforcement, and Replayable Assurance
entries.title: Authority-Inference Separation in Agentic Finance: First-Line Control, Blockchain Enforcement, and Replayable Assurance

entries.difference: Governs authority an agent acquires at runtime, for resources such as credentials and accounts; acquired authority is a flow the policy must contain, and it is orthogonal to the fidelity of an approval artifact.
entries.pool_title: Runtime Authorization for Resources Acquired by AI Agents
entries.title: Runtime Authorization for Resources Acquired by AI Agents

entries.difference: Binds a dependency closure and governs effects at operation time for agent skills; effect governance is a check on the operation, which is the repair axis this study prices.
entries.pool_title: Versioned Transitive Dependency-Closure Binding and Operation-Time Effect Governance for Agent Skills: ClosureBound
entries.title: Versioned Transitive Dependency-Closure Binding and Operation-Time Effect Governance for Agent Skills: ClosureBound

entries.authors: Hu, J., Goel, A., Bindschaedler, L.
entries.difference: Checks effects at runtime rather than trusting regenerated systems code; checking effects is one of the two repairs in this study's design ladder, and its value is measured here as a function of what the check can see.
entries.pool_title: Don't Trust the Code, Check Its Effects: Runtime Refinement for Regenerated Systems Code Under an Adversarial Generator
entries.title: Don't Trust the Code, Check Its Effects: Runtime Refinement for Regenerated Systems Code under an Adversarial Generator

entries.authors: Zheng, Y., Zhang, W., Mao, Y.
entries.difference: Argues agent capabilities should follow task intent and the source of context, so that authority tracks provenance; the argument is normative, and the value of the approval step it implies is what this study measures.
entries.pool_title: LLM Agent Capabilities Should Follow Task Intent and Context Source
entries.title: LLM Agent Capabilities Should Follow Task Intent and Context Source

entries.difference: Proposes an intent-aware control plane for policy-governed agentic systems; a control plane enforces policy at a boundary, and this study's unit is a single reviewer-mediated decision with a computable value.
entries.pool_title: Brain API: An Intent-Aware Control Plane for Policy-Governed Agentic Systems
entries.title: Brain API: An Intent-Aware Control Plane for Policy-Governed Agentic Systems

entries.difference: Studies delegating authorization to misaligned agents through coalitional alignment and safe control; misalignment is a property of the agent's objective, and the laundering channel here requires no misalignment, only an unfaithful artifact.
entries.pool_title: Delegating Authorization to Misaligned Agents: Coalitional Alignment and Safe Control
entries.title: Delegating Authorization to Misaligned Agents: Coalitional Alignment and Safe Control

entries.difference: Delivers prompt-space security skills to coding agents so that privilege use is mediated; it mediates the agent's own requests, while this study asks when a human-mediated mediation step has positive expected value.
entries.pool_title: SkillShield: Prompt-Space Security Skills for LLM Coding Agents
entries.title: SkillShield: Prompt-Space Security Skills for LLM Coding Agents

entries.difference: Anchors agent communication and human approvals in blockchain evidence for auditability; auditability after the fact is a separate good from the expected value of the approval the record attests.
entries.pool_title: A Black Box for Agentic Processes: Blockchain-Anchored Evidence for AI Agent Communication, Human Oversight, and GRC Audits
entries.title: A Black Box for Agentic Processes: Blockchain-Anchored Evidence for AI Agent Communication, Human Oversight, and GRC Audits

entries.difference: Estimates whether a model should act or defer to a human expert, and adapts deferral across experts; the deferral rule is the same structure as this study's escalation coverage, with the channel's fidelity held fixed and no harm term from an unfaithful review.
entries.pool_title: RACER: Role-Aligned Competence Estimation for Human-AI Routing
entries.title: RACER: Role-Aligned Competence Estimation for Human-AI Routing

entries.difference: Shows learning-to-defer reproduces algorithmic bias in the human it defers to; bias in the deferred-to label is a property of the reviewer's decisions, and our construct separates reviewer accuracy from the fidelity of the object reviewed.
entries.pool_title: Too Much of the Same: From Algorithmic to Human Bias in Learning to Defer
entries.title: Too Much of the Same: From Algorithmic to Human Bias in Learning to Defer

entries.difference: Predicts with an explicit reject option and communicates uncertainty; the reject option is escalation with no cost model, and this study's value is affine in coverage with a term for the mismatch escalation itself can introduce.
entries.pool_title: Epistemic Reject Option Prediction
entries.title: Epistemic Reject Option Prediction

entries.difference: Gives distribution-free error guarantees for classification with a reject option via conformal prediction; the guarantee is about the abstention rate, not about the net value of the escalated cases, which is what this study computes.
entries.pool_title: Classification with Reject Option: Distribution-free Error Guarantees via Conformal Prediction
entries.title: Classification with Reject Option: Distribution-Free Error Guarantees via Conformal Prediction

entries.difference: Extends selective prediction to distributional regression with a reject option; abstention is placed on a distributional target, and no channel between the reviewer and the executed object appears.
entries.pool_title: Distributional regression with reject option
entries.title: Distributional Regression with Reject Option

entries.difference: Asks what it takes to build a performant selective classifier; it measures abstention performance, where this study measures the value of the human who receives the abstentions and the fidelity of what they are shown.
entries.pool_title: What Does It Take to Build a Performant Selective Classifier?
entries.title: What Does It Take to Build a Performant Selective Classifier?

entries.difference: Audits whether models defer to a source-attributed cue and can be led to wrong answers; the cue's provenance affects the model, which is the mirror image of our reviewer trusting an unfaithful rendering.
entries.pool_title: When Models Defer to Wrong Answers: A Robustness Audit of Source-Attributed Cues in Multiple-Choice QA
entries.title: When Models Defer to Wrong Answers: A Robustness Audit of Source-Attributed Cues in Multiple-Choice QA

entries.difference: Gates a call to an LLM on confidence to control cost in emotion recognition; a confidence gate trades accuracy against cost, and this study's gate trades harm against the harm an unfaithful review can authorise.
entries.pool_title: When to Call an LLM: A Confidence-Gated Hybrid for Cost-Effective Emotion Recognition in Conversational AI
entries.title: When to Call an LLM: A Confidence-Gated Hybrid for Cost-Effective Emotion Recognition in Conversational AI

entries.difference: Decides when a failing robot should ask a human, given audited sensor evidence; asking is escalation, and the reviewed evidence is assumed faithful there, which is the assumption this study varies.
entries.pool_title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence
entries.title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence

entries.authors: Li, Z., Hara, T., Ota, J.
entries.difference: Decides whether, when and how to assist a user from scenario knowledge and thresholds; the decision is an intervention policy, and the object of the study is a gate whose input can misrepresent the action.
entries.pool_title: A Scenario-Knowledge-Driven Pipeline for Just-in-Time Assistance
entries.title: A Scenario-Knowledge-Driven Pipeline for Just-In-Time Assistance

entries.difference: Estimates confidence from experience so that a system can defer reliably; calibration of a self-report is a different object from the fidelity with which an approval denotes an action, and this study varies the latter.
entries.pool_title: Confidence Comes from Experience: Experiential Confidence Estimation from Reasoning to Agents
entries.title: Confidence Comes from Experience: Experiential Confidence Estimation from Reasoning to Agents

entries.difference: Places a human in the loop for nugget annotation and asks how the human is incorporated; incorporation design is a protocol choice, and the net value of the step is not derived there.
entries.pool_title: Human-in-the-Loop Nugget Annotation for Accountable LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations
entries.title: Human-In-The-Loop Nugget Annotation for Accountable LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations

entries.difference: Detects hallucination from complementary signals and frames false alarms as consuming limited human review capacity; that framing is this study's false-block cost, which enters its value law as an explicit term rather than as a motivation.
entries.pool_title: From Tokens to Semantics: Leveraging Complementary Signals for Hallucination Detection in Black-Box LLMs
entries.title: From Tokens to Semantics: Leveraging Complementary Signals for Hallucination Detection in Black-Box LLMs

entries.difference: Finds that a prior audit-repair context shifts an LLM verifier's threshold towards leniency; drift in a checker's operating point is the reviewer-accuracy axis, which this study holds fixed while varying fidelity, and the two are complementary.
entries.pool_title: Prior Audit-Repair Context Shifts LLM Verifier Thresholds Toward Leniency
entries.title: Prior Audit-Repair Context Shifts LLM Verifier Thresholds Toward Leniency

entries.authors: Lim, J., Shin, S., Hong, S.
entries.difference: Asks whether reasoning representations help humans evaluate model outputs; human evaluation quality is measured against a representation, which is a fidelity-like input evaluated for helpfulness rather than priced in a decision.
entries.pool_title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?
entries.title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?

entries.difference: Reduces over-refusal in LLMs with competing rewards, i.e. the false-block side of a filter; it optimises the rate, while this study asks when the harm from the other error makes a gate net-negative.
entries.pool_title: Addressing Over-Refusal in LLMs with Competing Rewards
entries.title: Addressing Over-Refusal in LLMs with Competing Rewards

entries.difference: Shows deepfake detectors learn some attack families less well than others; uneven detection across attack families is the same shape as a reviewer's effective sensitivity falling below its nominal one.
entries.pool_title: Not All Attacks Are Learned Equally in Speech Deepfake Detection
entries.title: Not All Attacks Are Learned Equally in Speech Deepfake Detection

entries.difference: Builds a guard model for unsafe or adversarial behaviour; a guard classifier is a programmatic reviewer, whose value under a defective channel is bounded by what it can see.
entries.pool_title: AprielGuard
entries.title: AprielGuard

entries.difference: Measures productivity and trust when people take, leave or fix human-AI collaboration outputs; the human's disposition is measured directly, and this study instead fixes the human and varies whether their information is faithful.
entries.pool_title: Take It, Leave It, or Fix It: Measuring Productivity and Trust in Human-AI Collaboration
entries.title: Take It, Leave It, or Fix It: Measuring Productivity and Trust in Human-AI Collaboration

entries.difference: Discusses complacency, comfort, relapse and distrust as side effects of automation in IoT; these are the dispositions that make a gate's value collapse, named qualitatively.
entries.pool_title: On the Side Effects of Automation in IoT: Complacency and Comfort vs. Relapse and Distrust
entries.title: On the Side Effects of Automation in IoT: Complacency and Comfort vs. Relapse and Distrust

entries.authors: Heinrich, D., McAndrew, I., Pretty, J.
entries.difference: Reviews human factors of satellite operations and interaction technologies; the domain is remote operation, and the treatment of the human is descriptive rather than priced.
entries.pool_title: Human Factors Considerations in Satellite Operation's Human-Computer Interaction Technologies: A Review of Current Applications and Theory
entries.title: Human Factors Considerations in Satellite Operation's Human-Computer Interaction Technologies: A Review of Current Applications and Theory

entries.difference: Enforces temporal constraints on LLM agents through guardrails; temporal safety is a constraint on the action, and this study's subject is a human step that may or may not have positive value under such a constraint.
entries.pool_title: Enforcing Temporal Constraints for LLM Agents
entries.title: Enforcing Temporal Constraints for LLM Agents

entries.difference: Audits approval integrity and recovery in one publication mechanism and reports a production response-act checker accepting 291 of 302 unsupported-labelled answers; that is one system's false-accept rate, where this study asks for the boundary at which the rate stops mattering.
entries.pool_title: Approval Integrity and Recovery in LLM Answer Publication
entries.title: Approval Integrity and Recovery in LLM Answer Publication

entries.authors: Shamis, A., Stephenson, M., Zhou, L.
entries.difference: Prices execution assurance for data-centre workloads in a BFT setting; pricing assurance is the closest economics to this study, but the priced resource is hardware-backed execution, not a human decision with a mismatch channel.
entries.pool_title: TEE-BFT: Pricing the Security of Data Center Execution Assurance
entries.title: TEE-BFT: Pricing the Security of Data Center Execution Assurance

entries.difference: Studies token economics for LLM agents from computing and economics views; it prices token consumption, and this study prices a human decision, whose harm term is absent there.
entries.pool_title: Token Economics for LLM Agents: A Dual-View Study from Computing and Economics
entries.title: Token Economics for LLM Agents: A Dual-View Study from Computing and Economics

entries.difference: Analyses software-based fault isolation empirically through controlled fault injection; isolation boundaries are enforcement mechanisms, and the object verified is code rather than an artifact a human approved.
entries.pool_title: Empirical Security Analysis of Software-based Fault Isolation through Controlled Fault Injection
entries.title: Empirical Security Analysis of Software-Based Fault Isolation Through Controlled Fault Injection

entries.difference: Formally verifies a software fault isolation system, including its verifier; a verifier proved correct is a different claim from a reviewer shown a faithful object.
entries.pool_title: Automated Formal Verification of a Software Fault Isolation System
entries.title: Automated Formal Verification of a Software Fault Isolation System

entries.difference: Layers several defences for LLM applications against prompt injection and related attacks; layering reduces attack success, and this study asks whether the human layer pays.
entries.pool_title: Countermind: A Multi-Layered Security Architecture for Large Language Models
entries.title: Countermind: A Multi-Layered Security Architecture for Large Language Models

entries.authors: Avina, A., Hariprasad, Y., Chaudhary, N.
entries.difference: Detonates malware in an ephemeral containerized sandbox; containment bounds the blast radius, which is an alternative to a gate rather than a value for one.
entries.pool_title: pokiSEC: A Multi-Architecture, Containerized Ephemeral Malware Detonation Sandbox
entries.title: PokiSEC: A Multi-Architecture, Containerized Ephemeral Malware Detonation Sandbox

entries.difference: Bounds the recall of a fixed-invariant FSA monitor by the entropy of the attack distribution; that is the adjacent monitor law for a programmatic detector, and no analogous bound is published for a human gate, which is what this study supplies.
entries.pool_title: Why Formal Monitors Fail: Attack Distribution Entropy as a Coverage Bound for LTL-Based LLM Agent Safety
entries.title: Why Formal Monitors Fail: Attack Distribution Entropy as a Coverage Bound for LTL-Based LLM Agent Safety

entries.difference: Formulates delegation authority as a POMDP and solves for a policy under uncertainty; the channel between delegate and delegator is assumed faithful there, and this study makes that channel its variable.
entries.pool_title: Adaptive AI Delegation under Uncertainty: A Bayesian Governance Policy for Sequential Decision Authority
entries.title: Adaptive AI Delegation under Uncertainty: A Bayesian Governance Policy for Sequential Decision Authority

entries.difference: Shows step-scoped monitors cannot detect compositional violations however accurate they are; the statement is that accuracy is not the axis for a monitor, and this study's statement is that fidelity, not accuracy, is the axis for a human gate.
entries.pool_title: Compositional Policy Violations: When Step-Level Compliance Fails In Agentic AI Workflows
entries.title: Compositional Policy Violations: When Step-Level Compliance Fails in Agentic AI Workflows

entries.difference: Reports that a checklist and a human-checked protocol reduced catheter-related bloodstream infections; a human verification step with a measured field benefit, which this study turns into a value that depends on the fidelity of what the checker sees.
entries.pool_title: An Intervention to Decrease Catheter-Related Bloodstream Infections in the ICU
entries.title: An Intervention to Decrease Catheter-Related Bloodstream Infections in the ICU

entries.difference: The meaning and use of the area under an ROC curve; the classical statement of what a reviewer's accuracy is, which this study holds fixed while varying the fidelity of the object reviewed.
entries.pool_title: The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
entries.title: The Meaning and Use of the Area under a Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve.
